intl.note: He supports a communication channel with China on AI ("I do think some channel on AI is necessary"; "But I do think engaging on this most important thing going on in the world right now is an important part of protection."), citing Cold War contact with the Soviet Union, but in the same remarks he rejected a pause because China would take the lead, and he said nothing in favour of an agreement on the pace of AI development. A Fox Business video caption (May 2026) says he condemned Sen. Sanders's call for US-China cooperation on AI regulation; no quote was available. He did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter. A reviewer should decide whether a communication channel alone counts; if not, this is "none".

record: Co-wrote an op-ed with Sen. Fetterman calling for stronger legal liability for AI companies and more federal oversight of models posing credible biological, cyber or nuclear risks, while opposing a slowdown and moratoriums.
The Free Press op-ed reposted on mccormick.senate.gov, 1 October 2026

Gave a speech setting out an AI framework: light regulation except for models with biological, cyber or nuclear risks, an industry standards body, child protections, and a data center 'covenant' instead of a moratorium.

In interviews on Fox News Sunday and 1210 WPHT radio, backed an industry-led oversight body modelled on the financial industry's self-regulator, further legislation placing liability on AI companies, a possible dedicated cabinet department for AI, and a communication channel with China on AI, while opposing a pause.
Sponsor, with Sen. Wyden, of the Remote Access Security Act to extend export controls to access to advanced chips through cloud services (aimed at China; not about AI safety).
Senate office press release (page dated 21 December 2025)
Co-sponsor of a Senate resolution led by Sens. Coons and Cotton on keeping US primacy in AI and limiting sales of advanced AI chips to China (about competition with China, not AI safety).
Did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter from 17 senators urging AI talks with China.
grade_reason: In a 1 October 2026 op-ed he named the growing dangers of biological, cyber and nuclear attacks and catastrophic harm from very powerful AI systems as real risks, and on Fox News Sunday on 20 September 2026 he listed bioterror as a possible risk of AI. The same op-ed calls claims that AI will kill us all hysterical, so he acknowledges catastrophic risk but rejects the extinction framing; all three B statements are borderline with C.
notes: Search complete: 8 web searches ran on 11 November 2026 (the six required ones plus two follow-ups); none was refused. An earlier run had covered only his own website; its four statements are kept unchanged. New material comes from one Center Square article (22 September 2026) reporting two interviews: Fox News Sunday (20 September 2026) and 1210 WPHT radio ('Friday', taken as 18 September 2026). The article does not say which interview the China channel and 'adequate controls' remarks came from; I dated them 18 September and flagged the statement unsure. I did not see a transcript or recording of either interview, so the wording is as transcribed by The Center Square. The Gateway Pundit (20 September 2026, https://thegatewaypundit.com/2026/09/senator-dave-mccormick-weighs-ai-race-china-video) transcribes the Fox bioterror line slightly differently ('disruption in the economy and the job market ... possibly in terms of bio terror'), so the exact spoken words should be checked against the video before publishing. All seven quotes were checked by a script to appear character for character in the linked pages (the four earlier ones on his site in the earlier run; the three new ones in the Center Square page in this run). The op-ed quotes 'We cannot dismiss workers...' and 'If a company develops...' also appear with the same wording (apart from the final punctuation mark) in The Center Square's report of the op-ed (https://justthenews.com/nation/states/center-square/fetterman-and-mccormick-team-how-regulate-ai); thefp.com itself shows only the opening of the op-ed without a subscription, so the full text was not checked there. The op-ed is co-written with Sen. Fetterman, so the words are jointly his. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (S. 5493, Sanders, with Rep. Casar in the House): no source seen showing McCormick co-sponsored it; coverage names no Senate co-sponsors, and congress.gov was not opened. Not verified either way. Pages that could not be opened (error 403): Axios, 15 April 2026 (https://axios.com/2026/04/15/mccormick-ai-revolution-risks-energy); Pennsylvania Capital-Star on his 18 May 2026 Pennsylvania Press Club speech; Mediaite on Nvidia chip sales. A search result said he is an original co-sponsor of the GAIN AI Act and the SAFE Chips Act (chip export limits on China); I could not open a page confirming this, so it is not in the record. Left out as level D: Axios event, 15 April 2026, 'That offers enormous opportunity, but it's also enormous disruption and risk, so it's scary' (read at https://okcfox.com/news/nation-world/republican-senator-dave-mccormick-says-ai-technology-could-cause-enormous-disruption; about economic and social disruption); Hudson Institute remarks reported by Nextgov on 19 October 2026 (permitting, energy and data centers only); speech line 'I am skeptical of both the doomers who predict mass unemployment' (jobs); 'America is in an existential race with Communist China' and the op-ed's 'If we cede AI leadership to totalitarian China, we risk surrendering our way of life' (competition with China); the Hudson Institute China speech on his site. Paraphrase left out: the Fox Business caption saying he condemned Sanders's call for US-China cooperation on AI regulation (video only, no text quote; date of remarks not shown). Several search results about an 'AI moratorium' concern Rep. Rich McCormick of Georgia, a different person, and were ignored. Judgment calls for the reviewer: the F label (the sentence rejects both extremes); B versus C for the three B statements; and whether support for a communication channel with China makes the international position 'mixed' or 'none'.
